input: Sign my kid up for a chess tournament

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The child's age, grade, and current skill level determine which tournament divisions or rating categories they are eligible for.
The preferred location (local, regional, online) and timeframe narrow down which specific tournaments are even viable options.
Whether the user wants help finding the tournament, just registering, or also preparing the child changes how much work is involved.
A budget cap affects which tournaments are feasible, since entry fees, travel, and equipment costs can vary widely.
Knowing whether the child already has a chess rating or membership (e.g., US Chess Federation) determines if that needs to be set up first before registration.
The desired tournament style (scholastic vs. open, casual vs. competitive, in-person vs. online) shapes which events are the best fit.
Understanding the goal — fun first experience, competitive ranking, social activity — determines what a 'good' tournament looks like for this family.

gold.taskTitle: Sign kid up for a chess tournament
gold.taskDescription: Register the user's child for an upcoming chess tournament, handling all necessary steps from finding the right event to completing the signup.

questions.title: How old is your child, and what is their skill level?
questions.description: The child's age and playing ability (beginner, club player, rated) determine which divisions or age brackets they qualify for.

questions.title: What location and timeframe work for the tournament?
questions.description: Knowing whether the family wants something local, regional, or online — and roughly when — narrows down real available events.

questions.title: Does your child already have a US Chess membership or rating?
questions.description: Many tournaments require a US Chess (or equivalent) membership number before registration; this determines if that step must happen first.

questions.title: What is your budget for entry fees and any travel costs?
questions.description: Tournament fees and associated costs vary widely; a budget sets a hard filter on which events are realistic.

questions.title: Do you prefer a scholastic event or an open tournament?
questions.description: Scholastic tournaments are age/grade-restricted and often more beginner-friendly; open tournaments include adult players and a wider rating range.

questions.title: Should this plan cover only registration, or also tournament prep?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the task ends at signing up or also includes steps like practice resources, gear, or day-of logistics.

questions.title: What does a successful first tournament look like to you?
questions.description: Whether the priority is fun, earning a rating, winning, or social experience shapes which tournament is the best match.
